newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks end bourse up, but Ifo caps gains.
newsitem.headline: German stocks end bourse up, but Ifo caps gains.

text.p: German shares ended bourse dealings higher on Wednesday, after Wall Street hit yet another record high, but gains were capped as a jump in a German business climate index undermined rate cut hopes, dealers said.

The DAX index of 30 leading shares closed floor trade up 10.41 points, or 0.38 percent, at 2,774.50, but the index did not manage to equal gains made in pre-bourse electronic trade as the release of the Ifo figure dampened sentiment.
The German Ifo index for October showed a higher-than-expected rise to 97.4 from 95.7 last month, pulling German bonds and pre-bourse share dealings lower.
Earlier, news that October German M3 money supply growth was steady at 8.4 percent had little effect on either bond or share markets.
"The market is lethargic. Nothing is moving very much, even Deutsche Telekom," said one trader.

The day's most heavily traded stock was Deutsche Telekom, which has led volumes since shares in the national telecommunications giant were first traded on Monday, although volumes were subsiding, dealers said.
Telekom ended bourse trade down 27 pfennigs to 31.80 marks, as investors continued to take profit.

Shares in steelmaker and diversified industrial group Thyssen AG rose most among DAX stocks, climbing over five percent or 14 marks to end floor trade at 283.50 marks, after the firm said its supervisory board would decide on Friday on plans to reorganise the group.

In contrast, the DAX's worst performer was industrial group Preussag AG, which fell over four percent after the company said profits for the business year that ended on September 30 fell sharply from the previous year.
Preussag shares ended down 14.50 marks at 359 marks.

Amongst the medium capitalised stocks, pharmaceutical group Merck KGaA gained ground after its nine month figures came out better than expected. Merck ended up two marks, almost four percent, at 56.75 marks.
Shares in specialty chemicals company SKW Trostberg AG and tyre maker Continental AG were also boosted by their respective nine month results.
SKW Trostberg closed up 1.49 marks to 42.89 marks, while Continental rose 98 pfennigs to 26.28 marks.
